sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border Physical Consignment of Shredded Non-Ferrous Scrap

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: France (Metropolitan France and overseas departments, unitary jurisdiction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, Articles 49-54 (freedom of establishment); Directive (EU) 2017/1132 on company law
France - People's Republic of China Double Taxation Agreement (signed 26 November 2013, effective 1 January 2015)
France - People's Republic of China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 26 November 2007)
France - Hong Kong Double Taxation Agreement (signed 21 October 2010, in force 1 December 2011)
OECD Model Tax Convention on Income and on Capital (interpretive framework)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Articles L.561-1 to L.561-50 and L.561-45 (AML/CFT obligations and freezing measures); Decree No. 2020-118 of 12 February 2020 (prevention of the use of the financial system for money laundering and terrorist financing); Code de commerce, Article L.123-28-1 (beneficial-owner statement filed with the Register of Commerce and Companies - RBE); Directives (EU) 2015/849 and (EU) 2018/843 as transposed; TRACFIN guidelines. Public access to the French beneficial-owner register is suspended following CJEU judgment of 22 November 2022 (C-37/20 and C-601/20); access is now restricted to competent authorities and AML-obliged persons conducting due diligence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the passport of each shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner (natural person)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary, consular office or licensed public certification authority of the shareholder's State of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the State is an Apostille Convention contracting party; otherwise consular legalization at the French Embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each UBO (utility bill or bank statement dated within the last 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or account-holding banking institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, followed by sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, memorandum of association, and register of directors of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or equivalent corporate registry authority of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source of wealth and source of funds declaration, executed before a foreign notary, accompanied by a bank reference letter
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign notary and the remitting bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization plus sworn French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate or judicial records extract for each UBO and for the intended legal representative (manager) of the SARL
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Justice or national police records office of the State of residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, managers, and counterparties against: (i) the national politically exposed persons file and asset-freeze orders administered by TRACFIN; (ii) the consolidated European Union financial sanctions list (CFSP); (iii) the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (iv) the OFAC SDN list, required for USD-denominated documentary credits and corresponding banking relationships; and (v) domestic French asset-freeze arrete. Screening must be repeated at onboarding, upon any change of UBO, and before each new counterparty transaction. Because the recycled non-ferrous scrap trade is classified Medium-Risk with enhanced due diligence, the compliance file must additionally apply CMF Articles L.561-4-1 and L.561-10-2 (written AML risk assessment, verification of the origin of funds), verify scrap suppliers' waste transport certificates, and observe the cash-payment ceiling of EUR 500 for professional purchases of non-ferrous metals imposed by the Code de l'environnement, Article L.541-7-3, and Decree No. 2011-960.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalites d'entreprises operated by INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), with name and prior-right verification via data.inpi.fr and Infogreffe (www.infogreffe.fr); the file is ultimately registered with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du commerce et des societes).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SARL name (denomination sociale) must be expressed in the French language under Law No. 94-665 of 4 August 1994 (loi Toubon). Any foreign-language word must be accompanied by a French translation in the articles and must be rendered in Latin-alphabet transliteration where the original script is non-Latin. The name must not be misleading as to the corporate object, must be distinguishable from names already registered in the RCS and from protected trademarks, and must not infringe public order. The name must be followed by the legal form indicator SARL in all commercial documents.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a stand-alone pre-incorporation name reservation; clearance is tested at the time of filing via the Guichet unique. A preliminary non-opposition certificate obtained through Infogreffe is commonly accepted by the Greffe as valid for 30 days, but no formal extension mechanism exists. Upon rejection: (i) request a written statement of grounds from the Greffe within 15 days; (ii) amend the name or add a distinguishing element and re-file without penalty; (iii) in case of conflict with a prior trademark, obtain a non-opposition or coexistence letter from the prior-right holder; (iv) if the refusal is procedural or unjustified, file a petition before the President of the Tribunal de Commerce (refere) to order the Registrar to proceed, within 30 days of the written notification; and (v) appeal any final judicial refusal to the Court of Cassation. Where the refusal is based on an INPI trademark opposition, the appeal must be lodged with the Cour d'appel within 2 months. Pre-incorporation defensive registration of the intended name as an INPI trademark is recommended to secure the name for 10 years and to support coexistence negotiations.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible, with conditions. A French SARL may domicile its registered office with an authorized commercial domiciliation company (societe de domiciliation agretee) under Code de commerce Articles L.123-11-2 and R.123-166. A virtual office is accepted for registration, tax correspondence, and legal notices. However, for a cross-border scrap-copper consignment trader, the company must retain operational substance: full accounting records and management documents must be accessible in France, and the registered address must accept customs, TRACFIN, and DGFIP notifications. Banks and financing counterparties will normally require a physical operating address or an accountant's substance letter when opening account relationships and agreeing documentary credit facilities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-High; quantified at approximately 20-30% annual probability of unannounced physical inspection during the first filed fiscal year. The sector profile, characterized by intra-Community acquisitions of non-ferrous scrap, high-value consignment flows, and the EUR 500 cash-payment ceiling under Article L.541-7-3 of the Code de l'environnement, makes the entity a target for coordinated inspections by DGFIP (tax), DGCCRF (trade and environmental enforcement), and customs authorities; environmental inspectors hold a statutory right of physical access under the waste-transport certification regime.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance, RCS availability verification, and trademark conflict search via INPI data.inpi.fr and Infogreffe
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI (Institut National de la Propriete Industrielle) and Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory online database access and search tariff; no formal registration fee for the preliminary verification

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Defensive pre-incorporation trademark filing of the intended company name (INPI, one class, electronic filing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff, approximately EUR 190 for a single-class e-filing, plus official fee adjustment

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization bundle for four UBO and shareholder documents (passport, address proof, corporate certificate, source-of-funds declaration)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostilling authority of the shareholder's State of residence, or French Embassy/Consulate for non-Apostille States
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory apostille/consular certification fees of the issuing State; international market benchmark for the four-document bundle

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn French translation of the notarized foreign document bundle (four documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator registered with a French Cour d'appel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of approximately EUR 80-120 per standard document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office domiciliation with an authorized domiciliation company (virtual office, 12-month contract)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed domiciliation company (Code de commerce, Articles L.123-11-2 and R.123-166)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of approximately EUR 550-700 per year plus VAT and client due diligence compliance fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the SARL Articles of Association (statuts), including the UBO annex, share transfer restrictions, and governance provisions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of approximately EUR 1,800-2,500 for a standard SARL under a fixed-fee engagement letter

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation notice in a licensed legal announcement gazette (Journal d'annonces legales)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed legal announcement gazette approved by the Prefecture
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory capped tariff for legal announcements; approximately EUR 210 average for a standard SARL incorporation notice

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS creation filing through the Guichet unique (INPI platform), including the beneficial-owner (RBE) statement
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI and Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du commerce et des societes)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory formalities fees: Greffe transcription fee of approximately EUR 37.80 plus INPI platform and e-payment taxes

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L223-1 to L223-43 and R223-1 to R223-36 governing SARLs; Articles L123-1 et seq. governing commercial registration; Articles L123-31 et seq. governing the national business register and the unified filing portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI); the competent commercial court registry (greffe du tribunal de commerce or designated commercial court) records the company in the Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic formalité de création, including the signed SARL articles of association, submitted through the Guichet unique; the filing results in registration in the Registre national des entreprises and, for a commercial activity, the RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital applies; EUR 1 is legally sufficient, although commercial adequacy must be assessed. At least 20% of cash contributions must be paid on incorporation and the balance within five years of registration. Cash contributions are deposited with a French bank, notary, or Caisse des dépôts et consignations before registration; deposited funds are released after issuance of the Kbis extract. In-kind contributions must be fully contributed at incorporation. The amount excludes the mandatory legal notice and variable professional or publication costs. The USD figure is an indicative conversion of applicable French registration and beneficial-owner filing charges and is not a fixed statutory USD tariff.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The undersigned shareholders and proposed management of [Company Name] SARL, noting that a SARL has no statutory board of directors, hereby resolve: (1) to approve the subscription and payment of the quotas stated in the articles of association; (2) to adopt [French address] as the registered office; (3) to appoint [name] as gérant for the statutory term, with authority to complete incorporation, banking, tax, customs, licensing, and registry formalities; and (4) to authorize opening the company bank account and executing documents required for commencement of the approved business. All actions taken in implementation are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm corporate identity, shareholders, management, and business activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique preparation interface and, where applicable, the competent mairie and prefectural services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the company name, registered office, SARL share capital, quota allocation, gérant appointment, beneficial owners, principal activity, secondary activities, and intended waste-trading or storage operations. Verify that the registered office permits the proposed activity and that the activity description covers physical consignment of non-ferrous scrap.
required_dossiers: Gérant identification documents and declaration of non-conviction and filiation
Detailed activity description and proposed premises information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistent activity codes, addresses, identification data, or beneficial-owner information before submission; obtain written landlord or domiciliation confirmation where the address is queried.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the articles of association and fund the share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French bank, notary, or Caisse des dépôts et consignations for capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Sign the articles in private deed form unless a notarial deed is legally required, including for certain real-estate contributions. Open a temporary company account, provide KYC documents and source-of-funds evidence, deposit at least 20% of cash contributions, and obtain the certificate of deposit. Use a sworn French translation where a foreign document is not accepted in its original language.
required_dossiers: Shareholder corporate documents and powers of attorney
Valuation report for in-kind contributions, or statutory waiver documentation where permitted
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to bank KYC requests, replace incomplete foreign certifications, and obtain an apostille or legalization where required. If the bank declines onboarding, use another eligible depositary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: An authorized Journal d'annonces légales publisher in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the statutory incorporation notice containing the company name, legal form, capital, registered office, term, activity, gérant details, and registration information required by French law. Obtain the attestation de parution and retain the publication invoice.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request immediate correction or republication if mandatory information is omitted, inconsistent with the articles, or published in the wrong department.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the creation formalité and beneficial-owner declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create the electronic filing, upload the signed articles, capital certificate, legal-notice attestation, registered-office evidence, gérant declaration, identification documents, and beneficial-owner declaration. Select commercial activity and request RCS registration. Pay the portal-assessed charges and electronically sign the submission.
required_dossiers: Foreign shareholder corporate records and powers of attorney, if applicable
Translations, apostilles, or legalizations where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Monitor the portal for a demande de régularisation, answer each query within the stated deadline, upload corrected documents, and preserve the electronic filing receipt. Escalate persistent technical issues through INPI support and the competent registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain registration evidence and activate tax, banking, and operational records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent commercial court registry, INPI, Service des impôts des entreprises, and the company's bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the SIREN, SIRET, NAF code, RCS registration, and Kbis extract. Provide the Kbis to the bank to release deposited capital and convert the account to an operational account. Confirm VAT, corporate-tax, payroll, and customs registrations according to the intended transactions. Register for EORI before importing or exporting goods.
required_dossiers: Payroll registration information, if employees are hired
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct NAF or activity-description errors through the INPI formalities channel, request tax-registration clarification from the relevant tax office, and suspend cross-border customs activity until the EORI is active.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-incorporation governance and compliance controls
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company gérant, shareholders, INPI, tax authority, customs authority, and relevant labor authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain the share-transfer register and accounting records, document shareholder decisions, preserve beneficial-owner data, and adopt written delegations for banking, customs, procurement, and environmental compliance. Establish AML, sanctions, counterparty, waste-origin, and transaction-traceability controls before accepting scrap consignments.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Record corrective shareholder decisions, amend the beneficial-owner filing when ownership changes, rectify accounting or tax records, and suspend transactions involving unverifiable origin, sanctions exposure, or missing waste documentation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The prefect of the department, acting through the Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL), for installations classified for environmental protection (ICPE). The relevant mairie and, where applicable, customs and waste authorities also exercise jurisdiction.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: ICPE declaration, registration, or authorization for the applicable storage, transit, sorting, or treatment installation, commonly including Rubrique 2713 for metals or metal-containing materials and potentially Rubrique 2714 or another waste rubric depending on waste classification, quantities, and site operations. A separate declaration as a waste trader or broker may be required under the French Environmental Code.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition and Territorial Cohesion, with the competent regional environmental authority and the prefecture; the environmental authority designated under the French Environmental Code conducts the applicable environmental review.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Site- and threshold-dependent. An ICPE declaration may require no full EIA; an ICPE registration or authorization may require an environmental examination, case-by-case screening, or full environmental assessment depending on the installation, quantities, processes, location, and applicable nomenclature thresholds. The final tier must be confirmed against the site-specific ICPE nomenclature before operations begin.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No single national threshold applies to every scrap-copper site. The applicable prefectural order and ICPE standard prescribe stormwater and wastewater controls, containment, sampling, noise, dust, firewater, and waste-storage requirements. Waste must be stored on impermeable surfaces with segregated and labeled areas; hazardous contamination must be assessed and managed under hazardous-waste rules. VOC limits apply only where relevant substances or processes trigger them. Waste traceability, including Trackdéchets where legally applicable, and transfer to authorized operators are required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain fire-prevention and emergency arrangements required by the applicable ICPE order, including extinguishing systems, access for emergency services, firewater containment where required, signage, staff training, and emergency procedures. Obtain building or land-use authorization from the mairie where construction or change of use is involved. Arrange structural, racking, loading-floor, electrical, and lifting-equipment inspections by competent qualified providers. Comply with the French Labour Code on risk assessment, workplace safety, machinery, personal protective equipment, occupational health, and employee training. A separate ERP public-accessibility and fire-safety approval is required only if the premises qualify as an établissement recevant du public.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), under the Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique; online professional portal at www.impots.gouv.fr (Espace Professionnel) and corporate formalities platform at www.formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr. Customs and export clearance authority: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI), with the DELTA electronic clearance system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the French SARL through the Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), which issues the statutory identity numbers (SIREN/SIRET) and registers the company at the RCS and with the INSEE. Step 2: Upon incorporation and before the first taxable transaction, the SARL files the notification form (M0) with the competent Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE), triggering the automatic assignment of the French VAT identification number (Numéro de TVA intracommunautaire, format FR + 11 digits/characters) and, where applicable, the EORI number for customs operations. Step 3: For non-resident entities without a French establishment that acquire goods or perform taxable B2B transactions in France, reverse charge applies; if direct VAT registration is required (e.g., local warehousing, distance sales above the EUR 10,000 EU threshold), the non-resident registers directly with the SIE (service des impôts des non-résidents) and obtains a standardized '0' SIRET. Step 4: The resulting VAT ID is validated through the European VIES database for cross-border B2B transactions and must be included on all invoices, customs declarations and the DEB (Déclaration d'Échanges de Biens). The SARL trading recycled copper scrap must additionally hold the statutory metal-purchaser registration (Registre des acheteurs de métaux, Code de l'environnement art. L.541-7), a precondition for valid purchased-invoice documentation and input VAT deduction.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (SARL default: corporate income tax, impôt sur les sociétés, at the French headline rate of 25%; reduced rate of 15% applies to the first EUR 42,500 of annual profit for small enterprises with turnover below EUR 10 million); Pass_Through_Eligible (small SARLs may elect income-tax treatment for 5 years under CGI art. 239 bis AA); Territorial_Scope (France applies the territoriality principle under CGI art. 209-I, taxing French-source profits of the French operation while foreign branch profits are generally excluded from the French corporate base, subject to documentation); Tax_Exempt_Zone (not applicable to the French mainland SARL; no free-zone status for this scrap-trading activity).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France has no US-style 'check-the-box' entity classification election. Available elections and statutory mechanisms: (1) Option for pass-through taxation under article 239 bis AA CGI for newly formed small commercial SARLs, irrevocable and limited to five fiscal years; (2) Option for corporate tax (IS) by otherwise tax-transparent entities under articles 206 and 239 CGI; (3) Group fiscal integration (intégration fiscale) under articles 223 A et seq. CGI by election of a 95%-or-more French parent; (4) The Union One-Stop-Shop (OSS) election for intra-EU distance sales of goods to consumers and the Import One-Stop-Shop (IOSS) election for imported consignments below EUR 150; (5) ATAD-based anti-hybrid measures under articles 209, 212 bis CGI and BOI-IS-BASE-35 neutralize hybrid mismatches without an election; foreign entity status is classified by the DGFiP using the 'comparison method' (BOI-IS-DEP-20-30).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA), transposing EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC into the French Code Général des Impôts (CGI arts. 256 to 298 nonies); customs duties and circular-economy contributions are administered separately by DGDDI.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de minimis registration threshold for established French domestic businesses; registration is compulsory from the first taxable supply. For small businesses, the franchise en base de TVA exempts sales of goods up to EUR 85,000 annual turnover (EUR 37,500 for services) with mandatory VAT registration above these limits; for intra-EU distance sales of goods, the harmonized EUR 10,000 threshold applies, after which the seller must charge the VAT of the destination Member State or elect OSS. Non-established foreign suppliers selling B2B goods to French VAT-registered customers are not required to register in France, as the customer applies the reverse charge; registration is triggered only for B2C distance sales, imports enabled by the IOSS option, or local warehousing operations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: French mandatory e-invoicing reform (OGD/En 16931 standard, format Factur-X/UBL/CII) is phased in from 1 September 2026 for large and mid-size enterprises and 1 September 2027 for small enterprises and SARLs. B2B invoices must be issued as structured e-invoices transmitted through a certified Partner Dematerialisation Platform (PDP) or the State Public Portal; B2C transactions in scope are covered by mandatory e-reporting of transaction data to DGFiP. Real-time fiscal clearance is effectuated through the platform network with structured e-invoice transmission, although France does not apply a pre-clearance digital stamping system to invoices; export transactions rely on the DGDDI DELTA electronic customs platform (DELTA-x/DELTA-G) for the Export Declaration DAE, with shipment data transmitted automatically for customs clearance and statistical risk management.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to destinations outside the EU qualify for definitive VAT exemption with full input VAT credit (true zero-rating) under CGI article 262-I, provided that: (a) the goods physically leave the territory of the EU within the statutory time limits; (b) the exporter (a French taxable person) holds valid transport documentation (B/L, CMR, AWB or multimodal document) evidencing exit; (c) a DGDDI-accepted export customs declaration (DAE) is made in the exporter's name; and (d) commercial documents precisely describe the shredded copper scrap under CN code 7404 with gross/net weight, alloy classification and transaction price. Intra-EU dispatches to VAT-registered customers are zero-rated under article 262-0 ter CGI upon validation of the customer's EU VAT ID and inclusion in the DEB/EC Sales List. Related export services (international transport, handling, inspection of the scrap cargo) qualify for zero-rating or the place-of-supply rules under articles 259 A to 259 D CGI. While French exchange-control regulations do not impose a strict statutory 180-day FX repatriation period for commercial exports, the 180-day benchmark is applied as the contractual/fiscal compliance window for documentary letters of credit, transfer-pricing documentation and anti-avoidance analysis for this operation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: DAE (Export Declaration accepted via DGDDI DELTA/DELTA-x electronic platform, authorised as a customs export declaration)
Bill of Lading (original or electronic, issued to the French exporter or its agent)
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank attestation of inward SWIFT credit/export proceeds domiciliation certificate)
Commercial invoice (complying with French invoicing requirements, CN code 7404, Incoterms 2020, quantities, unit prices)
Weight certificate and loading tally issued by an accredited weighbridge or SGS/Bureau Veritas inspection report
Sale contract and Incoterms clause evidencing transfer of risk and export responsibility
EU Exit Summary Declaration and/or arrival certificate at destination port/customs office evidencing physical exit from the EU
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP VAT reassessment rights extend to six years from the chargeable event (extended to ten years for real-estate and certain asset frauds), allowing the administration to claw back the zero-rated VAT as domestic VAT where export documentation is missing, insufficient, contradictory or the goods are found to have been diverted to the French or EU market. In addition to the VAT clawback, the penalty regime includes interest of 0.20% per month (intérêt de retard) plus: 40% penalty for bad faith (indemnités de mauvaise foi), 80% penalty for abusive manoeuvres, and a 50% erroneous-declaration penalty where the declared base is materially distorted (article 1788 A CGI). Deliberate fictitious or over-invoiced exports of scrap copper trigger criminal tax fraud sanctions under article 1741 CGI — up to 7 years imprisonment and a EUR 500,000 fine (or up to 75% of the evaded base) — and the DGDDI may impose customs criminal sanctions under the Code des douanes for misdeclaration or smuggling of goods governed by CN 7404, including confiscation of the shipment and fines of up to twice the value of the goods.

stage_3._legal_framework_note: All legal references refer to the Code Général des Impôts (CGI), Livre des Procédures Fiscales (LPF), Code de l'environnement (metal purchaser register) and EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC as applicable in the French Republic as of the effective date of this dossier; thresholds and rates are subject to parliamentary revision in the annual Finance Law.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, with ongoing coordination for exchange control oversight and capital reporting by the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions under EU Capital Movement Directive 88/361/EEC and the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (art. 63). There are no exchange control restrictions on profit or dividend remittance by a French SARL to non-resident shareholders, provided the company has duly filed its corporate income tax return, balanced the statutory annual accounts, and complied with anti-money laundering / beneficial ownership reporting obligations. Any capital inflow above EUR 15,000 must be reported to the French customs and tax administrations for statistical and anti-fraud surveillance under the French Monetary and Financial Code, but no prior administrative authorisation is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France does not impose any statutory export proceeds surrender requirement. A French SARL may freely hold export receipts in euro or foreign currency, whether on domestic or foreign accounts without conversion obligations. However, all export invoices and collection proceeds must be recorded in the statutory accounting books; any invoice exceeding EUR 100,000 must be itemised for customs/intra-EU statistical filing, and funds received on a French bank account should carry a compliant payment description referencing the underlying commercial invoice to facilitate cross-border verification.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account in EUR and Multi-Currency Envelope
Operational Account with FX and International Trade Services

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Trade Finance Account / Settlement Account
Operational Account and Documentary LC Facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for the core cross-border scrap settlement function. French-regulated electronic money institutions (e.g., Qonto, Treezor) can provide local EUR IBAN operating accounts for payroll and inventory expenses, but they generally cannot open documentary letters of credit, handle trade title documents, or support large USD/CNH wires for underlying physical consignments. Offshore EMIs that are not passported under PSD2 cannot legally solicit French clients or hold settlement funds for a French SARL; using an unauthorised offshore EMI to settle commercial trade debts may constitute illegal payment activity and expose the company to fines, seizure of funds, and refusal of VAT/tax deductions. Use a fully licensed French or EU-licensed bank for all trade payments, reserving fintech EMIs for ancillary domestic expenses.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The gérant (managing director) and each individual beneficial owner with at least 25% ownership must undergo a face-to-face or equivalent video-KYC interview with the French bank's compliance team. Most tier-1 French banks accept remote opening after production of notarised, apostilled corporate documents and a verified electronic identity check for EU residents, but for non-EU offshore shareholders they consistently require physical attendance of one director or presentation of a certified corporate pack at the bank's international desk. For the capital escrow phase, the depositing shareholder must sign an irrevocable blocked-deposit declaration in the physical presence of a bank officer or French notary before the SARL is formally incorporated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk non-ferrous metal trading (recycled scrap copper wire) flagged under ISIC 4669 and French AMF/KYC guidelines.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide full transaction-chain documentation: licensed supplier invoices, weighbridge tickets, material origin certificates (from European List of Waste / Annex IV), quality inspection reports, the SARL's internal AML risk assessment matrix, and signed environmental compliance evidence for the originating scrap yard.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident/offshore shareholder structure and potential opacity in ultimate beneficial ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a notarised and apostilled file containing the SARL's ownership diagram, passport copies of all natural-person shareholders, proof of address, adjudicated statutory declaration of source of funds, and a reference letter from the shareholder's primary regulated bank. For any intermediate holding entity, provide incorporation certificate, register of directors, and audited financial statements for the last three years.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, embargo or adverse media hits associated with the trade counterparty or clearing bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a real-time sanctions screening report covering OFAC, EU, UN, and national terrorist lists, an IP/domain intelligence check for all counterparty emails, and a signed anti-circumvention warranty. Retain copies of government-issued import/export licences, the EORI registration certificate, and the customs broker's licence to demonstrate legitimate cross-border flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient economic substance of the SARL in France, evidenced by no local office or local management.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the registered office lease or rental agreement, French telephone line, payroll registration for at least one resident employee, a bond of margin on scrap materials in a French customs warehouse, and a board resolution affirming that core logistics, invoicing and risk management decisions are made in France.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Initial share capital for the French SARL must be deposited into a blocked capital escrow account opened at a French bank, per Articles L.223-7 and R.223-4 of the French Commercial Code, before incorporation. The bank issues a certificate of deposit to the business registrar. For subsequent shareholder loans or equity top-ups, use a SWIFT MT103 wire from the non-resident shareholder's bank to the SARL's euro IBAN. The payment must clearly quote: (i) purpose code 'Capital Contribution or Direct Investment', (ii) the underlying board resolution authorising the injection, (iii) the shareholder's exact legal name matching KYC records, and (iv) a reference to the French capital transaction code 'FR-OPP' where required by Banque de France statistical declarations. For injections above EUR 15,000, the SARL must file the associated balance-of-payment statistical declaration electronically with Banque de France within 20 business days; all wires must pass through a French-authorised payment or credit institution and never through an unlicensed third-country EMI.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements should be executed through SWIFT MT103 for immediate TT settlement against scanned bills of lading and commercial invoice, or through an irrevocable documentary Letter of Credit under UCP600 (SWIFT MT700) for larger volumes requiring title document verification. For EUR-denominated domestic or intra-EU purchases, use SEPA Credit Transfer or TARGET2 settlement. Each outbound payment to the scrap supplier must include the SARL's corporate name, VAT/EORI registration, invoice number, material classification code, and country-of-origin reference in field 70. Payments must be released only after the verifying bank matches the beneficiary name to the original transport document consignee; proceeds may not be routed to a non-participant intermediary without an authenticated chain of endorsement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain Vanilla FX Forwards for EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/CNH, provided the underlying is a documented trade receivable or payable with maturity within the tenor
Cross-Currency Swaps for long-term non-EUR debt or capital commitment hedges
Currency Options (calls, puts and collar strategies) for price-protection against adverse EUR movement
FX Swaps for the temporary conversion of export proceeds into funding currencies

NDFs: Not permissible or structurally unavailable for EUR because the euro is freely convertible; any non-deliverable instrument referencing EUR/CNH is treated as unenforceable gambling unless transacted between two authorised credit institutions within France

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary general meeting and shareholders' approval of statutory annual accounts and allocation of result (approbation des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate records; minutes retained at registered office and made available to auditors, tax administration and RCS upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of each fiscal year-end; court-ordered extension may be granted upon petition by the manager
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unapproved accounts prevent the lawful RCS deposit; the manager may be held civilly liable and creditors or the public prosecutor may compel filing, with exposure to a civil fine and judicial winding-up if cessation of activity is inferred.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of approved annual accounts with the RCS, including balance sheet, profit-and-loss statement, notes and approval minutes (depot des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce through the Guichet Unique (INPI) / RCS registration portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of shareholder approval; if approval is not given, within one month of the expiry of the six-month approval period; extension available only by court order
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit may trigger a civil fine of up to EUR 5,000 per formal notice; repeated failure may lead the commercial court to order mandatory filing or strike-off (radiation) when combined with proof that the company has ceased trading.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and financial statement annexure (declaration de resultats and liasse fiscale)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Generale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) - Service des Impots des Entreprises at the registered-office tax centre
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year fiscal year: second business day following 1 May of the filing year. For a non-calendar or short fiscal year: within three months of fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic 10% late-filing penalty on net tax due, increased to 40% for bad faith or 80% for deliberate concealment or fraud, plus monthly late-payment interest at 0.8% per month and possible criminal fines for the manager.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return for the simplified-real regime (CA12/CA12E) covering taxable transactions of the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Generale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via professional online VAT service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Second business day following 1 May of each year for calendar-year taxpayers; entities under actual monthly or quarterly regime file by the 19th day after each period and file a final annual adjustment return under the schedule communicated by DGFiP
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late declaration subjects the taxpayer to a 10% surcharge on net VAT due, 40% for bad faith, 80% for fraud, plus statutory late-payment interest and, in serious cases, tax lien and criminal penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business contribution declaration (Cotisation Fonciere des Entreprises) for the French registered activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Generale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) - local business tax management; form 1327-CFE and associated statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed by the second business day following 1 May of the tax year; principal tax is assessed and payable by 15 December of the same year unless an electronic-payment schedule applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing causes a 10% late-filing penalty on the CFE base, a 40% penalty for known inaccuracies, plus statutory late-payment interest; unpaid CFE is secured by a legal privilege on movable assets.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory when, over two consecutive fiscal years, the SARL exceeds at least two of three thresholds: total balance sheet EUR 4,000,000; net turnover EUR 8,000,000; average workforce of 50 employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP in conformity with the Plan Comptable General (PCG) as interpreted by the Autorite des Normes Comptables; IFRS is permitted only for consolidated accounts, not for the SARL's individual statutory annual accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The initial UBO declaration is filed with the RCS at incorporation; any change in beneficial ownership, including a share transfer, must be declared to the RCS within 30 days and the internal UBO register updated. No standalone annual UBO confirmation form exists in France; the rule is a continuous updating obligation verified at each annual meeting and on any RCS event.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of corporate minutes and decisions (registre des decisions et assemblees)
Register of ownership and transfer of quotas (registre des mouvements de parts sociales)
Register of beneficial owners (registre des beneficiaires effectifs)
Register of managers and legal representatives (registre des mandataires sociaux)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 330 - USD 1,320 per year for professional domiciliation or registered-office services at a commercial address, excluding physical lease and utilities
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - USD 22,000 per fiscal year for a statutory certification by a registered commissaire aux comptes when the audit threshold is exceeded or an auditor is voluntarily appointed; simplified due-diligence engagements may start near USD 3,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporation tax (IS); 15% reduced rate applies to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit per fiscal year for qualifying SMEs (turnover below EUR 10 million and at least 75% of the share capital held by individuals or an SME).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Crédit d'Impôt Recherche (CIR); Crédit d'Impôt Innovation (CII); participation exemption under the mère-fille regime for qualifying 5%+ holdings (95% exemption); indefinite tax-loss carryforward under Art. 209 CGI, with an annual deduction cap of EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the excess; 3-year loss carryback available; no local business tax on trading margins (CVAE phased out for most turnovers); territoriality rule for foreign PE profits provided the DTA applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate income tax return No. 2065-SD (declaration de résultats) together with the liasse fiscale schedules 2050 to 2059-SD; mandatory electronic filing through the business portal 'Espace Professionnel' at impots.gouv.fr using the EFI/EDI protocol.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly or monthly instalment payments (acomptes) apply when the prior-year IS liability exceeds EUR 76,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Returns must be filed within 3 months of the close of the fiscal year. For a calendar-year SARL, the deadline is generally 3 May of the following year; where that date falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or public holiday, the deadline shifts to the first following working day.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit after restatement for non-deductible charges, tax adjustments, and integration of prior-year deficits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the full French-source profit of the SARL; no distinction for non-resident ownership applies to the tax base. Annex a schedule of carried-forward losses under Art. 209 CGI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year tax loss to be carried forward indefinitely (subject to the EUR 1,000,000 + 50% annual cap).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the deficit in the same return; no separate election is required. Losses are available to offset future French-source profits only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Boxes 366/367/368 – Base imposable au taux réduit (15%)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the eligible profit segment for the reduced 15% rate (first EUR 42,500 for qualifying SMEs).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The reduced rate is denied if more than 25% of the SARL’s capital is held by corporations or if turnover exceeds EUR 10 million; non-resident individual shareholding is included in the 75% individual-ownership test.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computed on the residual taxable base at the standard rate of 25%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the standard rate to the amount remaining after the 15% reduced-rate tranche; no specific non-resident rules alter the computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Recoverable tax credits, including CIR, CII, and any withholding-tax credits arising from foreign-source income attributable to the SARL.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders have no claim to CIR/CII; verify that the SARL retains the supporting expense documentation and the underlying R&D or innovation invoices.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an automatic 5% surcharge on the tax due if filed within 30 days of the first formal notice, 10% after 30 days, 40% where a formal assessment is issued for deliberate omission, and 80% for abusive obstruction; late-payment interest accrues at 0.20% per month; fixed fines of up to EUR 150 per missing or incomplete schedule (Art. 1728 CGI; Art. 1731 CGI).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% outbound withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident corporate shareholders (Art. 119 bis 2 CGI); non-resident individuals are subject to a 12.8% withholding tax within the 30% prélèvement forfaitaire unique (PFU); the rate rises to 75% for dividends paid to persons established in non-cooperative States (ETNC).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The beneficial owner must deliver a residence certificate (attestation de résidence fiscale, Form 5001 for dividends, 5002 for interest, 5003 for royalties) to the paying SARL prior to the payment date; the SARL then applies the reduced DTA rate and files the certificate with the tax authorities; for EU corporate shareholders, the Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption (0% WHT) applies if the shareholder holds at least 5% of the SARL’s capital for a minimum of 2 years and files the same Form 5001 with proof of the holding period; the payer must retain the certificate for 6 years for audit purposes.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-residents: domestic withholding 33.33% (Art. 182 B); treaty rates typically 0-10% and 0% for qualifying EU associated companies under the Interest-Royalties Directive (2003/49/EC) with a 25% direct or indirect link. Interest on shareholder loans (comptes courants d’associés): domestic withholding 30% (Art. 125 A); treaty rates typically 10%; interest deductible only where arm's-length substance is established and thin-cap rules are satisfied.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full Local File and Master File are mandatory where the French entity or its ≥50% parent exceeds EUR 400,000,000 in either annual turnover or gross balance sheet assets; smaller SARLs are not exempt from the obligation to hold contemporaneous evidentiary documentation (invoices, contracts, margin analyses) and are subject to simplified documentation upon audit; all cross-border transactions with entities in non-cooperative States (ETNC) trigger the full documentation requirement regardless of turnover.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) code comparable to offshore regimes, but economic substance is tested through the general anti-abuse rule (abus de droit, Art. L. 64 LPF), the definition of permanent establishment, and the OECD BEPS Action 6 principal purpose test (PPT) incorporated into French DTAs. The SARL must demonstrably maintain local management, commercial premises, logistics oversight, headcount, and an auditable contract chain for the recycled copper wire trade; a letterbox or conduit structure interposed solely to divert French-source trading profits will be re-characterised and treaty benefits will be denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration of scrap copper trading revenues, fabrication of purchase invoices, use of unrecorded cash sales, concealment of foreign bank accounts, or misclassification of taxable commercial income as treaty-exempt passive income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 1741 of the French Tax Code: up to 5 years' imprisonment (7 years where committed by an organised gang) and a fine of up to EUR 500,000; the tax administration issues a re-assessment plus late-payment interest at 0.20% per month and penalty surcharges of 40% for bad faith or 80% for fraudulent manipulation; criminal confiscation of assets is available.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be prosecuted personally; joint and several civil liability for the company's tax debts is imposed under Art. L. 267 LPF for manœuvres frauduleuses or grave and repeated tax-law violations; applicable consequences include asset freezes, travel bans, passport confiscation, and imprisonment for resident and non-resident directors alike.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Shell / Abuse of Law (Abus de droit)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SARL is established or interposed with no genuine economic substance, such as no local decision-making, no physical operations, no staff, or a passive routing structure designed to shift recycled-scrap trading profits to a low-tax jurisdiction or to claim treaty benefits on dividends, interest, or royalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-characterisation of the arrangement under Art. L. 64 LPF with an 80% penalty on the recomputed tax base plus monthly late interest; the abusive scheme is voided for tax purposes, and dividends, loans, or fees are reclassified as taxable distributions or deemed income; the authority may also re-file a criminal complaint for fraudulent declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly design or validate the artificial arrangement face personal joint liability for the entire reassessed tax and penalties; travel bans and director disqualification may be imposed; criminal prosecution under Art. 1741 for tax evasion is possible, with up to 5 years' imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Handling cash payments for scrap copper above the legal threshold, accepting untraceable bearer instruments, failing to identify the true beneficial owner of the supplier, refusing to file a suspicious-transaction report (SAR/STR) to Tracfin, or structuring transactions to avoid the EUR 10,000 cash-payment reporting threshold in a medium-risk enhanced commercial environment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Articles 324-1 to 324-5 of the French Penal Code: up to 5 years' imprisonment and a fine of EUR 375,000 for legal entities; administrative sanctions by the ACPR/AFA may include fines up to EUR 100,000 or 10% of turnover; the prefectural commercial licence for regulated scrap dealing may be suspended or withdrawn; confiscation of the SARL's assets is mandatory for proceeds of crime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be indicted for money laundering and conspiracy; personal assets may be seized; professional bans and travel bans are commonly imposed; non-resident directors may face extradition requests under bilateral treaties; the failure to implement an adequate AML compliance programme constitutes an aggravating factor.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance and Transactions with Non-Cooperative States (ETNC)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Unjustified margin stripping, excessive management fees, non-arm's-length pricing for copper wire sales to a related buying entity, absence of contemporaneous TP documentation, or payments in the form of interest, royalties, or service fees to a parent in an ETNC without substance and without an accurate economic analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-assessment of the French taxable base; penalty of 40% for bad faith or 80% for abusive scheme; specific sanction of 5% under Art. 1732 CGI for failure to produce TP documentation; payments to ETNC recipients lose deductibility under Art. 238 A CGI, and a 75% withholding tax is applied to dividends, interest, and royalties paid to such recipients (Art. 119 bis 2 bis, Art. 125 A, Art. 182 B CGI); cumulative interest at 0.20% per month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the reassessed tax whenever they directed the transfer pricing policy or neglected the obligation to maintain documentation; criminal exposure under Art. 1743 for obstruction of fiscal audit adds further risk; administrative sanctions may include a bar from management duties and a travel ban for non-resident directors.
